title: The Quiet Bakery
premise: Marine biologist Rosalind Pemberton has spent eleven years in a coastal town, tending a quiet bakery by dawn and counting sea turtles by day, convinced she can train her heart into containment after the accident that took her sister and her fiancé's trust. When a letter postmarked eleven years ago surfaces—her sister's final words, delayed by a dead-letter office—Rosalind learns her sister knew about the affair that broke them all, and forgave it. As Rosalind tracks down everyone the letter touches, including the man she never stopped loving, she must decide whether justice means punishment or truth; she ends the story choosing confession over silence, reopening both the bakery's back room and her heart, as the turtles finally nest.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories with salt still on their hands. She lives above a bakery she refuses to name, where she claims the best plots arrive at 4 a.m.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Flour
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet her double life: pre-dawn baking, turtle surveys, and rigid routines designed to keep feeling containable. A postal worker delivers a water-stained letter postmarked eleven years ago—her sister Maren's handwriting. Emotional beat: controlled grief cracked open by an impossible arrival.

chapters.title: What Maren Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Rosalind and flashbacks to Maren. The letter reveals Maren knew about Rosalind's engagement to Daniel colliding with her own secret—and forgave them both before dying. Rosalind seeks out Daniel, now a widowed coast guard officer, who believed Rosalind blamed him. Emotional beat: guilt reframed as shared survival.

chapters.title: The Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV mostly. He and Rosalind work the turtle patrols together, circling each other while the town's found family—the bakery regulars, the postal worker, Maren's old friend—push them toward honesty. Rosalind discovers Maren's death involved a cover-up by the marina owner. Emotional beat: rising tension as private forgiveness meets public injustice.

chapters.title: Proof Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. Rosalind exposes the marina owner's negligence at a town hearing, choosing truth outside the courts, then gives Daniel Maren's letter unedited. In the bakery's back room, they grieve together and choose each other; the season's first hatchlings make for the sea. Emotional beat: release—justice rendered, heart retrained toward openness.
